checks.name: E1-글로벌 이슈 현재성
checks.detail:
rank=2: inaccurate — Briefing dramatically understates the situation. This is not a lingering ~18% traffic reduction with stalled talks — multiple sources (Wikipedia '2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis/campaign', Atlantic Council, CNBC) describe an active US-Israel-Iran war since Feb 28, 2026 (following an Israeli/US strike that killed Iran's supreme leader), with traffic 'largely blocked', a US Treasury oil waiver just revoked, and on July 31 itself Iran's IRGC struck two US-escorted tankers in the Strait, prompting four more vessels to turn back. Oil (Brent/WTI) is up ~20-22% for the month on this. The 'developing / de-escalation talks stalled' framing is misleadingly mild for what is an active shooting war directly moving oil markets same-day.
    rank=3: outdated — Google's search antitrust remedies were already decided by Judge Mehta back in September 2025 — and notably the court REJECTED structural relief in favor of behavioral remedies (data/index sharing, no exclusive Gemini/Chrome/Assistant distribution deals), contradicting the briefing's claim that DOJ is 'seeking structural remedies' now entering a phase with September hearings. Separately, the FTC's Meta monopolization case was dismissed by Judge Boasberg (TikTok/YouTube counted in market definition) and is on appeal — no corroboration found for a 'Meta Llama open-source licensing' remedy track. Could not verify the specific WSJ 7/31 / NYT 7/30 filings cited.

global_issues.title: US-China chip export controls shift to case-by-case licensing
global_issues.note: Confirmed: BIS final rule effective Jan 15, 2026 moved review of H200/MI325X-class exports to China from presumption-of-denial to case-by-case, conditioned on US third-party testing, a 50%-of-domestic-sales volume cap, and a 25% tariff routed to Treasury. Matches briefing closely.

global_issues.title: Iran-Hormuz tanker traffic remains disrupted amid Red Sea spillover
global_issues.note: Briefing dramatically understates the situation. This is not a lingering ~18% traffic reduction with stalled talks — multiple sources (Wikipedia '2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis/campaign', Atlantic Council, CNBC) describe an active US-Israel-Iran war since Feb 28, 2026 (following an Israeli/US strike that killed Iran's supreme leader), with traffic 'largely blocked', a US Treasury oil waiver just revoked, and on July 31 itself Iran's IRGC struck two US-escorted tankers in the Strait, prompting four more vessels to turn back. Oil (Brent/WTI) is up ~20-22% for the month on this. The 'developing / de-escalation talks stalled' framing is misleadingly mild for what is an active shooting war directly moving oil markets same-day.

global_issues.title: DOJ/FTC AI antitrust probes enter remedy phase for Google/Meta
global_issues.note: Google's search antitrust remedies were already decided by Judge Mehta back in September 2025 — and notably the court REJECTED structural relief in favor of behavioral remedies (data/index sharing, no exclusive Gemini/Chrome/Assistant distribution deals), contradicting the briefing's claim that DOJ is 'seeking structural remedies' now entering a phase with September hearings. Separately, the FTC's Meta monopolization case was dismissed by Judge Boasberg (TikTok/YouTube counted in market definition) and is on appeal — no corroboration found for a 'Meta Llama open-source licensing' remedy track. Could not verify the specific WSJ 7/31 / NYT 7/30 filings cited.

missing_major_news.impact: Direct driver of the 10Y topping 4.7% (highest since Jan 2025) and 30Y hitting 5.25% (highest since 2007) — the exact rates weakness the briefing's sector section flags for TLT/TNX, but the causal Fed event itself is never mentioned.

missing_major_news.title: Active IRGC tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz on July 31 pushed oil sharply higher (Brent ~$90, WTI ~$85, +20-22% on the month)
missing_major_news.impact: Contradicts the briefing's sector claim that Commodities (GLD/OIL/BTC) are uniformly RED/weak — oil and gold were both UP on the day this crisis is actively escalating. Relevant to any energy-exposed watchlist names.

missing_major_news.title: Micron (MU) selloff driven by CXMT (Chinese memory maker) stock debut and HBM oversupply/margin fears, plus Michael Burry increasing his short
missing_major_news.impact: MU: explains the -5.9% to -3% move in the watchlist, but the underlying competitive-threat narrative (Chinese memory entrant) is absent from the briefing.

market_mood_check.note: VIX level (~16) and the 'green'/risk-on tone are directionally consistent with the actual tape (S&P +0.7%, Nasdaq +1%, Dow +0.5% on July 31). But calling Hormuz a lingering 'risk' that markets are shrugging off is misleading — it is an active war with same-day tanker strikes and a 20%+ monthly oil spike; the mood summary undersells the geopolitical severity even if equities happened to close green that day.

sector_check.note: Rates (TLT/TNX) RED is well-supported (yields at multi-decade/multi-year highs post-Fed). But 'Commodities (GLD/OIL/BTC) all flash RED, reflecting... weaker commodity momentum' is factually wrong for two of three: gold rose ~1.2% and oil (WTI/Brent) rose >1% on July 31 specifically because of the Hormuz tanker attacks, with a ~20-22% monthly gain. Only Bitcoin (slipped below $63k) was actually weak that day.

grok_report.summary: The chip-export item is accurate, but the Hormuz item severely understates an active shooting war that is the actual driver of a 20%+ monthly oil spike, and the antitrust item misstates case posture (Google's remedy was already decided as behavioral, not structural, nearly a year ago). The sector commodities call is factually backwards on oil and gold, and the Fed's July 29 hold — the real cause of the rates weakness the briefing does cite — is never mentioned. Watchlist price moves (AMZN, AAPL, MU) are broadly consistent with real earnings-driven action.
